clue.text: Caption rewritten to protect leader of Lords Spiritual

indicators.note: the shuffled letters surround and so shield the single letter, which sits inside them
text that is rewritten has its letters set down again in a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter, here from Lords

explanation.surface: A caption is redrafted so as to shield the head of the Lords Spiritual, the bishops in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords Spiritual' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits it: Lords supplies L, and Spiritual alone is the definition. 'rewritten' shuffles CAPTION into PATONIC, and 'to protect' wraps it round the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic love is spiritual rather than physical, so the two adjectives describe the same non-sexual bond.

clue.text: One's honour in life less if solitary

indicators.note: the honour group goes inside what is left of life
the letters of if are subtracted from life

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone's honour means less in a life of solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' leaves LE once the little word is struck out, and 'in' sets the honour group between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome means lonely or isolated, the condition of someone solitary.

clue.text: Flavouring rib and leg with salt

parts.note: a tar or Jack Tar is an old sailor, a salt
to rib and to rag both mean to tease
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A cook seasons rib and leg of lamb with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib', 'leg' and 'salt' look like a butcher's order; ON, the leg side, is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is a herb whose leaves flavour sauces such as béarnaise.

clue.text: English lecturer raised point

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: An English lecturer brings up a point in a seminar.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a point where lines or branches meet, as in a network.

clue.text: Dodgson right in tune with literature initially

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the tune

parts.note: a carol is a song or tune

indicators.note: the first letter of literature

explanation.surface: Dodgson was right in step with literature from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, author of Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Author secretly wore tights to dance

indicators.note: letters made to dance jump about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer covertly put on tights to go dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a book that appears under someone else's name is to author it without credit, hidden from readers.

clue.text: Material from Derbyshire depressed chap

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed
John is any man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A miserable man is made of Derbyshire stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county in the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue John is a purple-banded fluorite mined only near Castleton in Derbyshire, used for ornaments.

clue.text: You could say we admitted to sick satire

indicators.note: the pronoun is let inside the shuffled satire
sick letters are disordered, mixed up

explanation.surface: We were let in to watch a sick satire, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges SATIRE into ASITRE, and 'admitted to' puts WE in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning so to speak, flagging that words are used loosely.

clue.text: Old warrior pilots circling raised ground

indicators.note: the pilots fly round the ground, so their letters go around it

parts.note: aces are expert fighter pilots
a hill is a piece of raised ground

explanation.surface: An ancient soldier watches airmen fly in circles above a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek hero of the Trojan War, the warrior of Homer's Iliad, so very much an ancient fighter.

clue.text: Butter in hospital leaving taste less refined

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes away from the word for taste

parts.note: a hint is a slight taste, as in a hint of garlic
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
ruder means coarser, less polished

explanation.surface: Some butter in hospital, leaving a cruder taste, as if from a grumble about hospital food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the spread, but it is one who butts in. 'leaving' strips the hospital letter to give INT.
explanation.definitionFit: One who butts in pushes in uninvited, which is exactly what an interloper or trespasser does.

clue.text: House physician makes chief executive powerless

indicators.note: the word for power, abbreviated to its letter P, is left out

parts.note: a president is the chief executive of a republic or company

explanation.surface: A hospital's house doctor manages to strip the chief executive of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' means losing P, the physics abbreviation for power, from PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a junior hospital doctor living on site, the kind of post Britain calls a house physician.

clue.text: He wrote line about good companion

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on birds
a fellow is a companion or comrade

explanation.surface: A writer pens a line about a good friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: Old prince at graveside finally choosing body

parts.note: an elector was a German prince entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor

indicators.note: the last letter of graveside

explanation.surface: An old prince stands at the graveside at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of voters, the people who choose representatives.

clue.text: Medical man with drill causing misery

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
PE, physical education, is drill or exercise at school

explanation.surface: A doctor wielding a drill would cause anyone misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' suggests a dentist's tool, but here it is school exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mope is a gloomy, listless person, a misery in the colloquial sense of a wet blanket.

clue.text: Heroic lover with piercing sidelong look

indicators.note: the word for with goes through the middle of the look

parts.note: a leer is a sly sidelong glance
and means together with

explanation.surface: A romantic hero casts a penetrating sidelong glance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his beloved Hero, so he was literally Hero's lover.

clue.text: Row about books possibly disheartened retired printer

indicators.note: the row goes around the inner group

parts.note: a line is a row
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the two letters go backwards
a word losing its heart keeps only its outside letters, from possibly

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over books, possibly from a downcast retired printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps the outer letters of possibly, 'retired' turns them round to YP, and 'about' wraps the row around the inner group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Linotype was a hot-metal typesetting machine, a printer's machine casting whole lines of type.

clue.text: Cleverly sculpted statue likely to be hollow

indicators.note: sculpted letters are reshaped into a new form
a hollow word keeps only its outside letters, from likely

explanation.surface: A cleverly carved statue will probably turn out hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: To act astutely is to act shrewdly and sharply, with cleverness.

clue.text: Gag first couple from Lebanon, smuggled in after

indicators.note: the two letters are slipped secretly inside the other word

parts.note: since can mean after, as in ever since the war

indicators.note: the first two letters are taken from Lebanon

explanation.surface: A gag order follows a smuggling operation out of Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'since' as 'after' is the fair stretch: ever since the war means in the time after it. 'smuggled in' tucks the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to silence them, the verb in both cases meaning stop from speaking.

clue.text: One million central to assets — that's a rough guess

indicators.note: the pair sits in the middle of the assets word

parts.note: an estate is the total assets left by a person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Valuing assets at a million is only a ballpark figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation, a rough guess at a figure.

clue.text: Opening cold beer, expose rabble

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the beer is cut open and the other word put in it

parts.note: ale is beer
to nail a lie is to expose it

explanation.surface: Cracking open a cold beer shows up the riff-raff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like popping a can, but it means the beer is split for the exposing word to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille is a French-derived word for the mob, the common people seen with contempt.

clue.text: Golden vegetable seen in cultivated land

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A golden vegetable grows in a tilled field.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is ground planted with fruit trees, a piece of cultivated land.

clue.text: Military alliance in collision at once

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words collision at once

explanation.surface: An alliance of armies suddenly finds itself in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is the Western military alliance founded in 1949.

clue.text: Oily substance from tree put in ground with nitrogen

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A tree is planted in soil with nitrogen fertiliser, yielding an oily resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is the anagram signal: TREE, PUT IN and N for nitrogen are all rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a volatile oil distilled from pine resin, used to thin paints.

clue.text: Joint ruler and poet wanting start on time

indicators.note: the poet's name lacks its opening letter

parts.note: Petrarch was the Italian sonnet poet

explanation.surface: A co-ruler and a poet are waiting for the time to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting start' drops P from PETRARCH, and T for time goes on before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrarch ruled one of four divisions of a Roman province, so shared rule with others.

clue.text: Game found by river — deep but not wide

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: the wide letter is excluded from the deep word

parts.note: low means deep, as a low voice
W is a wide in cricket scoring, a ball out of the batter's reach

explanation.surface: A game turns up by a river that is deep but narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team game played on horseback with mallets.

clue.text: Charming area within reach across river

indicators.note: the achievable word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: doable means achievable, within reach

explanation.surface: A charming spot lies within reach on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is delightful and lovable, which is what charming means.

clue.text: Column only remaining in support for bridge

indicators.note: the remaining word goes inside the support

parts.note: a pier is a pillar holding up a bridge span
the last one is the only one remaining

explanation.surface: Only one column remains standing in a bridge support.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting from a wall, a decorative pillar.

clue.text: Cynic — one involved in swindle — means to inherit

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the swindle

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
I is the Roman numeral one
genes are how traits are inherited

explanation.surface: A cynic gets caught up in a fraud as a way to come into an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynic with a capital C is a philosophical school, not a sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope, who lived in a barrel, was the most famous Greek Cynic philosopher.
